in_greek.name: Κλαρένζα
in_greek.meaning: Χριστιανικό όνομα που σημαίνει καθαρό και φωτεινό
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κλαρένζα είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό και σημαίνει καθαρό και φωτεινό. Είναι συνδεδεμένο με την έννοια του φωτός, που αποτελεί κεντρικό θέμα στον Χριστιανισμό. Το όνομα αντανακλά την πίστη στο φως του Θεού που φωτίζει τις καρδιές των πιστών.

in_english.name: Clarenza

in_english.long_meaning: The name Clarenza is of Latin origin, meaning clear, bright, and shining with divine light. Etymologically, it is linked to the Latin word 'clarus,' meaning clear or bright. This name is significant in Christian tradition as it reflects the spiritual concept of being illuminated by God's light. Historically, names with similar roots have been used to signify purity, hope, and spiritual enlightenment. The name Clarenza embodies these qualities, symbolizing a person who brings light and clarity to others. In modern Christian cultures, the name is chosen for its beautiful meaning and melodic sound.

historical_references.reference: Clarence I, Duke of Naples, was born around 1264 and ruled from 1268 to 1285. He was the second son of Charles I of Anjou, who held the duchy of Naples, Sicily, and Hungary at the time. Clarence was given the name Clarenza in honor of St. Clare of Assisi, whom his mother, Beatrix of Provençe, was especially devoted to.
historical_references.context: House of Anjou, Italy, Sicily, Hungary

historical_references.reference: Clare of Assisi (1194-1253), was a significant figure in the early history of the Franciscan Order. She renounced her wealthy family life to join St. Francis of Assisi and became one of the first women to be recognized as a saint in the Catholic Church. The name Clarenza, which means 'clear' or 'bright', may have been inspired by her remarkable spiritual clarity and the radiance of her faith.
